title: Classify frames, subsample them, and run a TDNN layer
brief: Stack frames into context windows, compute exact convolution output lengths, build a 4x Conv2d front end, train a frame classifier on noisy synthetic phones, and run a time-delay layer with its receptive field.
hints: np.arange(T)[:, None] + np.arange(-left, right + 1)[None, :] gives a (T, window) index; np.clip it to [0, T - 1] and index the features once.
Write the length formula with // so it works unchanged on ints, numpy arrays, and integer tensors.
In Conv2dSubsampling.forward, x.unsqueeze(1) makes (N, 1, T, F). After both convolutions the shape is (N, C, T', F'); transpose(1, 2) then reshape(n, t, c * f).
The linear layer's input size is channels * subsampled_length(n_mels): frequency shrinks the same way time does.
Pass raw logits to F.cross_entropy; it applies log-softmax itself.

tdnn_layer keeps only frames t where t + min(offsets) >= 0 and t + max(offsets) <= T - 1. Index x with frames[:, None] + offsets[None, :], reshape to (n_frames, len(offsets) * D), and multiply by weights.T.
A layer with offsets {-3, +3} extends the window 3 frames left and 3 right. Add left extents over layers and right extents over layers; a layer whose offsets are all positive extends the left by 0.
